title: fix(memory): recover file watching after worker crashes
body:
## Problem

An unexpected exit of the shared Memory file watcher worker permanently stopped file observation until the Gateway restarted. The failed transport also erased watcher health, so this could appear healthy while missing edits.

## Change

Keep supervision in the existing shared watcher transport. An unexpected exit logs a warning and publishes unavailable/degraded health, then retries after 0.5, 2, and 5 seconds. Each replacement receives every live subscription and uses the existing watcher baseline reconciliation to catch edits missed during downtime and rebuild shared-root selection/exclusion unions. Four failures within a rolling minute stop automatic restarts and retain explicit unavailable health with restart guidance. Searches keep the existing background refresh fallback; recovered ready health clears that fallback.

Final subscription shutdown cancels recovery and joins native cleanup, worker exit, and accepted indexing. Closed subscriptions are not replayed. The old permanently failed transport path is removed. This adds no SQL, schema, SDK, or main-thread filesystem scan.

Accepted edge case: changes during backoff are eventually indexed by the replacement's baseline rescan. Persistent worker failure requires explicit lifecycle restart after the bounded retry budget. No security-boundary checks were removed or weakened.

## Measurement

Runtime: Node v24.22.0, SQLite 3.54.0. All six arms passed their recorded causal coverage, runtime/build identity, SQL-error, ledger reconciliation, and fixture cleanup checks.

Values are median [min–max]. Warm values pool individual turns; whole and phase values use three run totals per side. Raw windows include overlapping background work; causal values follow each turn across threads.

Memory attribution includes execution and request-origin frames, then all SQL belonging to the matching request IDs. Its directly executed SQL shapes stay identical across all six arms (333 statements); the complete closure additionally includes shared registry work. C3 skips two registry snapshot SELECTs during archive sync. M3 omits one zero-SQL deferred Memory prewarm request. Neither is claimed as a saving.

Raw warmed MAIN peaks come from the same 13 startup plugin-maintenance lease reads per workload moving between first-turn and warmed windows. Whole MAIN varies only by startup busy-timeout setup/restoration; no watcher MAIN SQL is introduced. All five shared read families have zero observed raw or causal warm SQL, and their whole-workload medians do not rise.

### Attribution and limits

Causal first-turn SQL stays 180, while requests are 53 [53–54] → 54 [53–54]. Both request totals occur on both revisions. The three varying first-turn request origins are unchanged ACP metadata (+1 median), callback dispatch (+1), and transcript-worker tasks (−1), explaining the net +1. Whole causal-turn requests remain median 386. Raw first-turn medians decrease 360/101 → 337/100 SQL/requests; combined boot+connect+first decreases 942/218 → 925/217.

Compaction+settle totals are M: 379/58, 380/58, 379/58 and C: 379/58, 378/58, 377/58 SQL/requests, all MAIN0. Combined restart decreases 630/193 → 605/193. The only rising nonwarm raw SQL phase medians are connect (+2) and restart-boot (+3); both are within +10 statements and +2%, with lower adjacent combined windows.

Raw warm position01 rises 70→87 SQL even though the pooled raw and causal warm medians stay unchanged. Its +17 is accounted for by +4 transaction-envelope statements, +8 lease-expiry reads, +1 machine-state upsert, +2 machine-state reads, +1 lease deletion, +2 busy-timeout settings, and −1 catalog snapshot write. These startup/background operations are unchanged by this PR. Every workload has the same 13 post-ready MAIN lease reads; only their phase placement differs.

Whole SQL decreases mainly because untouched transcript-index restart maintenance (34 SQL/1 request) runs in all three baseline arms and only C2. Whole requests rise by 2 (+0.218%); the exact median arms M3/C3 reconcile as transcript tasks +3, state reads −2, catalog snapshot +1, update sentinel +2, callback dispatch −2, zero-SQL Memory prewarm +1, session entry patch −1, transcript worker resources −1, ACP metadata +1. These origin groups explain the observed difference; they are not independent semantic-owner costs. The touched Memory request median remains 49. No SQL saving or latency improvement is claimed.

## Validation

- Focused transport and manager regressions cover real worker termination, downtime edits, restored extra-path subscriptions, shared-root member retirement, crash-loop exhaustion, startup retry, recovered search behavior, and joined shutdown.
- Local changed-file formatting/lint and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2 (one round). Original-head CI passed all 14 cases in the three changed test files, types, lint, source contracts, Madge (zero cycles), T1/dialect ratchets, and both PostgreSQL conformance shards. Final integrated-head CI also passed all 14 changed-file cases, types, lint, source contracts, Madge, and the T1/dialect ratchets. Canonical Knip completed all three scopes on the final candidate and frozen baseline: the same 9 production, 8 full-tree, and 1 script findings, with zero new or changed-file findings. Both PostgreSQL conformance shards passed on the final head. [Final CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39019766824) is terminal with only the inherited cache-overflow case and aggregate gate red. The [published-driver × candidate lifecycle update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39019768547/job/117362715829) passed on the full final SHA. Its broader package workflow fails only the independently tracked npm12 installed-entry budget (48,202 versus 47,500); the actual update cell passed, and the shipped updater cap is 50,000.
- Original-head CI also failed the untouched `manager.reindex-recovery.test.ts` case `bounds the shadow cache before any entries reach the primary` with `primary cache overflow`. A focused replay fails identically on the original main base and candidate; this inherited failure is recorded for the cache owner. No assertion or capacity limit was weakened.
- Review disposition: the comment claiming that the accepted-indexing close test deterministically rejects overlooks the initial attachment await and synchronous worker-exit cleanup; that exact test passed both original and final CI. No behavior change is warranted.
- The existing PostgreSQL watcher fixture correction is included in the baseline and remains unchanged.

The added production state is limited to one active worker, its exit/failure result, live subscription membership, and a bounded retry timer/history; existing observation and indexing owners continue to do the work. Diff against base: production +176/−83 (net +93); tests +190/−35 (net +155); docs +7. Merged as `de2349923e273ff2639c86ae991eaea95605bb42`; the six changed files exactly match the reviewed candidate. The measurement series is complete. No SQL savings or wall-time improvement is claimed.
